channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Italy evacuates hundreds of schools after receiving email bomb threats
item.description: At least 300 Italian schools on Wednesday were evacuated after receiving emailed bomb threats, the country's education minister said.

item.title: Pope Leo to end Argentina tour with large outdoor mass before 'emotional' Peru homecoming
item.description: Pope Leo will conclude his three-day visit to Argentina on Wednesday with an outdoor mass expected to draw millions, before traveling to his hometown of Peru. The pontiff plans to give a speech to Peruvian president Keiko Fujimori, whose election earlier this year was marred ‌by fraud accusations and vote-counting delays.

item.title: Russia, Ukraine start second day of US-led talks: Kyiv lead negotiator
item.description: Russia and Ukraine have resumed US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi for a second day, Kyiv's chief negotiator Rustem Umerov said on Wednesday.

item.title: French journalist Christophe Gleizes marks 500 days in Algerian jail
item.description: Pierre de la Saussay, a friend of Christophe Gleizes, is our guest.

item.title: Second day of Web Summit cancelled as Storm Charles puts Portugal on high alert
item.description: Portuguese authorities strongly advised organisers of the Web Summit to cancel events this Wednesday because of risks of tidal flooding and severe disruption to public transport. Storm Charles is expected to be at its most dangerous on Wednesday afternoon, with winds reaching up to 120 km/h and potentially very dangerous wind gusts as well.

item.title: Angry Nemo : clown fish becoming more agressive because of climate change
item.description: Listen to Theresa Rueger, Senior Lecturer in Tropical Marine Biology.

item.title: Spain's first general strike in 14 years, 3 weeks before national polls
item.description: Sarah Morris is live from Madrid.

item.title: Lewandowski ordered to preserve records related to his time at DHS by key Democrat
item.description: Former DHS advisor Corey Lewandowski ordered to preserve all records related to his time at DHS by incoming Senate Committee Chair

item.title: Iran-backed trio accused of plotting attacks on U.K. base hosting U.S. jets
item.description: Iran-backed operatives have been charged over nearly 20 attacks, including a plot on a U.K. base housing U.S. troops. Separately, a U.S. soldier is held in the U.K. on Russia spying claims. (Image credit: Alastair Grant)

item.title: Portugal shuts schools, tech conference as it braces for storm
item.description: Portugal said it would shut schools, non-essential services and a top world tech conference on Wednesday, as it braces for gale-force winds of Storm Charles.

item.title: Oil giant ExxonMobil left Venezuela years ago. Now it's considering a return
item.description: ExxonMobil has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Venezuelan government and its state-owned oil company to explore opportunities in the country. (Image credit: Brendan Smialowski)

item.title: AI hoaxes are deceiving 911 dispatchers, and they're only getting harder to detect
item.description: Swatters are increasingly using AI technology that creates synthetic voices or sound effects to generate remarkably believable fake emergency calls to law enforcement. (Image credit: Alex Edelman/AFP via Getty Images)

item.title: Volunteer musicians play songs for veterans who are hospitalized
item.description: Volunteer musicians play for veterans and others who are hospitalized. They're part of Musicians On Call, a group that spreads the healing power of music. (Image credit: Tyrone Turner/WAMU for NPR)

item.title: U.S. officials look to Europe to learn how to make prison better
item.description: American prison officials are looking to European nations like Germany and Norway for a roadmap on how to design a prison that emphasizes rehabilitation and a successful return to life on the outside. (Image credit: Lena Mucha)

item.title: Nayib Bukele says Salvadoran troops destroyed gang HQ in Haiti
item.description: President Nayib Bukele said Tuesday that Salvadoran troops deployed to Haiti had destroyed the headquarters of one of the Caribbean nation's most powerful gangs.Bukele has deployed more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti since late October, after four Salvadoran troops went missing in the country.

item.title: House Republicans quash effort to impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth
item.description: Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi, our international affairs editor, has more.

item.title: Spain's first general strike in 14 years demands solutions to housing crisis
item.description: Less than three weeks before a national election that could catapult the far right to power, Spain's workers are striking on Wednesday to demand that the government remedy the nation's housing crisis. (Image credit: Francisco Seco)

item.title: Africa: Ghana waste dump poses health, environmental 'crisis'
item.description: An acrid haze hung over a sprawling dump in Ghana's capital, Accra, as excavators gouged into mounds of smouldering rubbish. Thin plumes of black smoke curled from burning plastic and rubber, mingling with the rank odour of stagnant lagoon water.

item.title: UK authorities arrest US soldier suspected of spying for Russia
item.description: A member of the US army suspected of spying for Russia was arrested in Britain on Tuesday, London police said, following an investigation with support from the American military and law enforcement.

item.title: Four children among those in hospital after car collides with pedestrian
item.description: Four children were among those injured after a car collided with a number of pedestrians in Glasgow.

item.title: Football: Éli Junior Kroupi earns first France call-up from Zinédine Zidane
item.description: Bournemouth centre-forward Éli Junior Kroupi has earned his first call-up to the French national team. He replaces Marcus Thuram, who is injured and has been returned to his club Inter Milan.

item.title: Ebola tops 11,000 cases in Congo's deadliest outbreak
item.description: Congo's Ebola outbreak has topped 11,000 cases, the government said Wednesday, a stark figure that underscores the severity of the situation as the country grapples with the relentless spread of the disease. (Image credit: Sebastien Kitsa Musayi)

item.title: Police address 'violent incident' claim against Russell Brand made by Jemima Goldsmith
item.description: Police have addressed an alleged "violent incident" involving Russell Brand after claims made his then-girlfriend Jemima Goldsmith.

item.title: Tech consultant sentenced to 16 years to life in stabbing death of Cash App founder
item.description: The tech consultant convicted in the stabbing death of Cash App founder Bob Lee has been sentenced in San Francisco to 16 years to life to prison

item.title: Want to live on the moon? NASA opens recruitment for Artemis programme
item.description: NASA is expanding its astronaut corps for the first time in two years. As the US space agency grows its Artemis programme, recruitment is in progress for a brand-new class of space explorers who will train to "live and work beyond Earth".

item.title: Spain’s general strike puts housing crisis at centre of upcoming elections
item.description: Millions of Spanish workers are striking Wednesday – the first general strike in 14 years – to demand action on a major housing crisis and the rising cost of living. The expected disruptions to public transport and the widespread closure of businesses come less than three weeks before a snap election that could bring the far right to power.

item.title: Teddy Riner candidacy 'illustrative of hunger for alternatives' to France's Le Pen or Mélenchon
item.description: As Teddy Riner throws his hat in the race for the French presidency, amid France's sociopolitical and economic crises, François Picard is pleased to welcome Lex Paulson, Director of Executive Programs at UM6P School of Collective Intelligence at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University. The prospect of Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner entering France's presidential race raises questions that extend well beyond the political ambitions of a celebrated and beloved athlete.

item.title: French far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 presidential race
item.description: Far-right pundit Eric ⁠Zemmour on Tuesday officially announced he will run for the French presidency. A politician with a prominent anti-Islam and anti-immigrant ​stance, he vows to "preserve a French France".

item.title: Trump's lawsuit against BBC can go ahead, judge rules
item.description: The BBC's attempt to have Donald Trump's $10bn (£7.5bn) defamation claim thrown out has been dismissed by a Florida court.

item.title: Missing 11-month-old boy taken by father rescued after being buried alive: Sheriff
item.description: The baby, Koah Sharpe, was found Tuesday afternoon "clinging to life," after spending what is believed to have been 24 hours buried, according to authorities.

item.title: Live: Zelensky welcomes inclusion of Europe in US-mediated peace talks
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Wednesday welcomed the inclusion of Europe in the US-mediated negotiations being held in Abu Dhabi, adding that it "was not simple" to involve representatives from the bloc. Though the second day of talks is now over, Ukraine said earlier that its negotiators would hold a separate meeting with the EU. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: US charges three men allegedly linked to RAF Fairford incident
item.description: Three men have been accused by US authorities of being Iran-supported operatives who plotted more than a dozen attacks, including an alleged terrorist plot near a UK military base where American aircraft were stationed.

item.title: Four grizzly bears killed mother and daughter in Canada
item.description: Four grizzly bears captured in Canada were responsible for killing a mother and daughter earlier this month, officials have said.

item.title: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah faces prison as trial sparks international outcry
item.description: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah, head of independent news outlet Mada Masr, faces a criminal court retrial Wednesday over charges of operating without a licence and publishing false news. The UN criticised Egypt’s “widening assaults on press freedom” Tuesday. Attalah was previously handed a one-year prison sentence in absentia in 2024.

item.title: Boat capsizes off Senegal's northwest coast, leaving 39 dead
item.description: At least 39 people have died after a migrant boat capsized off Senegal, one of the country's deadliest migration tragedies in recent years. We try to understand why so many are still willing to put their lives at risk, with our guest Aissata Kane from the International Organization for Migration.

item.title: Haiti's PM praises Bukele after Salvadoran troops help destroy gang headquarters
item.description: Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé praised Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele on Tuesday after Salvadoran troops aided in the destruction a suspected gang leader’s home near Port-au-Prince. Bukele’s deployment of more than 2,000 soldiers following four Salvadoran troops’ disappearance has raised concerns over rules of engagement and coordination with a UN-backed force combating Haiti’s gangs.

item.title: WATCH: Video shows rescue of girl nearly swept away by wave in Oregon
item.description: As powerful waves hammer the Oregon coast, video shows the dramatic rescue of a child pulled into the surf by a so-called "sneaker" wave.

item.title: Democratic lawmakers want answers on 8-year-old Haitian boy taken into ICE custody
item.description: A group of Democratic lawmakers is seeking information from the Trump administration after an 8-year-old Haitian boy was taken into government custody last week.

item.title: House Republicans elect Jim Jordan as minority leader for the next Congress
item.description: House Republicans on Tuesday elected Jim Jordan as minority leader for the next Congress, beating Majority Leader Steve Scalise, according to multiple sources.

item.title: Teddy Riner candidacy 'illustrative of this hunger for an alternative' to Le Pen or Mélenchon
item.description: As Teddy Riner throws his hat in the race for the French presidency, amid France's sociopolitical and economic crises, François Picard is pleased to welcome Lex Paulson, Director of Executive Programs at UM6P School of Collective Intelligence at at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University. The prospect of Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner entering France's presidential race raises questions that extend well beyond the political ambitions of a celebrated and beloved athlete. At a time when traditional parties are struggling to mobilize voters and the political center has all but collapsed, Riner's emergence points to a broader transformation of French politics: the growing importance of personal credibility and the capacity to embody an alternative prioritising people over the system.

item.title: Trump ally Jim Jordan elected House Republican leader after midterm defeat
item.description: Congressman Jim Jordan, a hardline ally of President Donald Trump, was elected House Republican leader on Tuesday, defeating Steve Scalise 106-73 in a secret ballot, US media reported. He replaces Mike Johnson after Republicans lost both chambers of Congress in last week’s midterm elections and will lead the party’s opposition.

item.title: Jimmy Carter's family farm to be preserved and opened to the public
item.description: The family farm where President Jimmy Carter tended peanuts, corn and sugarcane as a boy and returned throughout his life will be preserved and opened to the public

item.title: Thomas Markle's mugshot released after 'he cut off tag'
item.description: Thomas Markle is back in custody in the US after being accused of cutting off the electronic ankle tag monitoring his movements while under house arrest.

item.title: House panel rebukes DOJ's handling of Epstein case
item.description: The House Oversight Committee, in a report summarizing its 15-month Jeffrey Epstein probe, rebuked the Justice Department's handling of the Epstein case.

item.title: Ex-investigator admits depriving war crimes probe of potentially valuable information
item.description: A former senior investigating officer for the Royal Military Police has admitted depriving a war crimes investigation of potentially valuable information.

item.title: Iran live updates: Hegseth says Trump 'kicked their teeth in'
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.description: ABC News’ Chief Meteorologist Ginger Zee has some eye-opening demonstrations she hopes can help save lives during flash floods.

item.title: UK court overturns Trinidad and Tobago law criminalising homosexual sex
item.description: ‌Trinidad and Tobago's ‌law criminalising consensual sexual ​relations between male same-sex couples has been overturned ‌by a ​UK court.

item.title: Sophie visits refugee camps on trip to Bangladesh
item.description: Sophie has visited the Rohingya refugee camps at Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh to see the support being offered to displaced people from Myanmar.

item.title: Supreme Court lifts pause on border construction in Big Bend, Texas
item.description: The construction will include physical walls, access roads and vehicle barriers, according to Trump administration plans.

item.title: WATCH: Officer shot 6 times celebrates wedding
item.description: Five months after Buffalo Police Officer Marc Hurst was shot six times while on duty, he celebrated a moment that once seemed far from certain: marrying his fiancee, Haley.

item.title: WATCH: Woman living the 'dream' to save foxes in need
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a woman who's on a mission to save foxes at a sanctuary in upstate New York.

item.title: Police officer dies and another seriously injured after explosion in northern Spain
item.description: One police officer has died and another has lost a leg after an explosive device detonated at the scene of a shooting in northern Spain.

item.title: California's Prop 40 'billionaires' tax' measure is rejected, AP projects
item.description: The tax was introduced in response to steep cuts to California's healthcare funding that resulted from the passage of President Donald Trump's "Big Beautiful Bill."

item.title: At least 12 killed in Bulgaria motorway pile-ups involving dozens of vehicles
item.description: At least 12 people have been killed in two motorway pile-ups in eastern Bulgaria, the country's health minister said.

item.title: FBI investigating Nvidia CEO over affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description: Donald Trump has said the FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy - but insisted he is a "very honourable man".

item.title: WATCH: 'Love is Blind' season 11, Erika Kirk: Here's what's trending
item.description: ABC's Rocsi Diaz takes a look at what's buzzing, including the Netflix series reunion not holding back and Erika Kirk speaking out after Dave Chappelle joked about her husband's assassination.

item.description: ABC News' Rebecca Jarvis reports ahead of the Vikings' Salute to Service game as running back Aaron Jones earns a nomination for the NFL's Salute to Service Award.

item.description: Disney kicks off the holiday season with a new short film called, “A Disney Holiday Short: The Invisible Horse.”

item.title: DOJ leadership shakeup continues as Civil Division chief steps down
item.description: The head of the Justice Department's Civil Division, Brett Shumate, has submitted his resignation, becoming the latest DOJ leader to step down following the midterms.

item.title: France blames Iran for massive cyber attack on supermarket fridges
item.description: France has accused Iran of being behind the massive cyber attack on supermarket fridges last month.

item.title: WATCH: Vikings superfan has only missed 2 home games in 25 seasons
item.description: “GMA” is outside U.S. Bank Stadium with Minnesota Vikings “Fan of the Year,” Lindsey Lorenston, as she is surprised with a pair of tickets to Super Bowl LXI.

item.description: Harrison Fields served as the White House principal deputy press secretary from January to August 2025.

item.title: WATCH: Family's gigantic fern named 'Jeff' goes viral on social media
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a family in Colorado who has an annual tradition of having to move their gigantic fern, named Jeff, back inside for autumn.

item.title: Explosion at steel plant in Turkey kills 16, president says
item.description: A major fire broke out following an explosion at an iron and steel plant in Turkey on Monday killing 16 people, the country's president confirmed.

item.title: At least 14 dead after boat carrying migrants found near Crete
item.description: At least 14 people have died after a boat carrying migrants was found near Crete, Greek authorities have said.

item.title: WATCH: NASA recruiting next generation of astronauts
item.description: NASA has released a new recruitment video, looking for new space explorers as it works to create a permanent base on the moon and someday possibly launching humans to Mars.
